nodes.label: AuthorizationGate
nodes.rationale: Single enforcement point for all 49 authenticated Recommerce endpoints; decides on two independent facts - the permission is catalogued in config('recommerce.permissions') AND granted to the user via $user->can(). Chosen as a single seam so no service re-implements the permission half.

nodes.label: CohortPolicy
nodes.rationale: Deny-by-default: empty or incomplete cohort configuration must always deny access, so an unset RECOMMERCE_COHORT_BUSINESS_ID can never read as matches-anything.

nodes.label: Deny-by-default cohort contract
nodes.rationale: RC-006 requires deny-by-default; two mutation survivors (matchesConfiguredId, variationIsConfigured returning true for unconfigured input) showed the promise was correct in code but unverified by any test, so a refactor could have flipped it silently with a green suite.

nodes.label: RecommercePermissionGatekeepingTest
nodes.rationale: Structural guard owed since RC-006, blocked for weeks by RC-041's bypass. Enforces four rules: no inline authorisation primitive, anything naming a catalogued permission must reference AuthorizationGate, only the gate and the role editor may read config('recommerce.permissions'), and the one DataController exemption must contain no authorisation primitive. Reads the catalogue by require-ing the config file rather than config() so narrowing tests cannot silently shrink what it checks, and asserts >30 entries so an empty catalogue turns it red rather than passing vacuously.

nodes.label: RecommerceBoundaryTest
nodes.rationale: Pins the catalogued-vs-granted quadrant that RC-041 fell into, and guards config/label parity for every catalogued Recommerce permission.

nodes.label: LegacyRepairArchiveService
nodes.rationale: Injected AuthorizationGate but never called it - checked only that the permission string was listed in config plus CohortPolicy::allowsBusiness, never $user->can(). Confirmed by execution as a live privilege escalation while the full suite was green, because the only permission test defined the user's can() as in_array($ability, config('recommerce.permissions')) - the same condition the buggy service checked.

nodes.label: RC-041 legacy repair archive
nodes.rationale: Blocked for three reasons: it contradicted the RCR-001 UNAVAILABLE/INSUFFICIENT-EVIDENCE Repair disposition, it could not satisfy its own acceptance criteria without licensed Modules/Repair source (archiving the transaction shell alone would create a false record of completeness), and it carried an authorization bypass. Later authorized and reworked onto AuthorizationGate as an evidence-limited, scoped archive adapter.

nodes.label: RC-006 authorization regression sweep
nodes.rationale: Swept all 51 Recommerce endpoints, 18 controllers and 23 services to test whether the missing-$user->can() defect was systemic; it was a one-off in unlanded work. Services with no gate calls were individually confirmed non-authorizing helpers/writers.

nodes.label: RC-038 trade-in acquisition
nodes.rationale: Deterministic versioned pricing, structured evidence, approval gates, a one-unit native purchase seam, append-only acquisition/reversal history and a server-rendered UI. Release approval remains blocked because reversal has no UI to prove it in a browser.

nodes.label: RC-033 repair quote endpoints
nodes.rationale: quotes.store/.send/.decide are referenced by no view, so the documented diagnose -> quote -> approve -> work workflow cannot be performed and RepairQuoteService::assertWorkAuthorised never fires. Not built here because a quote form needs product decisions and inventing them would put fabricated business rules into a POS.

nodes.label: RC-039 warranty claims
nodes.rationale: Recorded as 'UI smoke pending' when in fact there was no UI at all - service and route existed but nothing referenced them. Landed at 7d5adbc after review; policy_version deliberately left NULL because the snapshot hardcodes version_number = 1, so policy versioning is nominal rather than implemented.

nodes.label: RC-002 platform certification
nodes.rationale: Run against a clean git-archive HEAD export rather than the dirty tree so the blocked RC-041 migrations could not contaminate the certified baseline. Certifies install/migrate/boot/route/test on PHP 8.2.33 + MySQL only - not load, security, or browser.

nodes.label: RCR-001 baseline report
nodes.rationale: Records the Repair disposition as UNAVAILABLE / INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE and forbids implementing any Repair source, route, migration, permission, version, attachment or production-data migration decision under RCR-001.

nodes.label: RCR-010 RC-038 trade-in acquisition decision
nodes.rationale: Decision 2 defers settlement to native UltimatePOS payment flows, with ownership transferring when the purchase posts even while still 'due', and requires the native payment record to reference the offer by valuation UUID rather than putting device data in free text.

nodes.label: TradeInService
nodes.rationale: Never creates a Device and never writes a DeviceIdentifier, so duplicate strong identifiers are prevented structurally rather than by validation.

nodes.label: Unreachable trade-in reversal
nodes.rationale: TradeInService::recordReversal is implemented, permission-gated, requires a matching native purchase_return and is tested, yet has no route, controller action or view. The outstanding browser reversal proof is therefore impossible as built, not a scheduling problem. Building the UI needs a decision on how the native purchase-return reference is supplied and confirmed, so it was recorded rather than invented.

nodes.label: Native settlement proof
nodes.rationale: Money moves in POS, nothing moves in Recommerce: paying an accepted trade-in's purchase through the native TransactionPaymentController wrote one transaction_payments row and flipped payment_status to paid, while every trade-in-scoped Recommerce row came back byte-identical including lock_version. Turns RCR-010 decision 2 from claim into evidence.

nodes.label: An empty comparison is not evidence
nodes.rationale: Two empty dumps compare equal, so an 'UNCHANGED' verdict can fire on nothing at all; the corrected check counts rows on both sides and reports 'NO ROWS - not evidence'. Same trap as an assertion that only checks no open prior period remained, which passes just as happily if the rows were deleted outright. Also: do not seed between a snapshot and the measurement.

nodes.label: Mutation-check every guard
nodes.rationale: Several tests written passed while proving nothing until mutated, and surviving mutants turned out to be findings about the code rather than gaps in the test. Confirm the mutation actually landed - two runs silently failed to patch the file (shell escaping) and reported a false pass.

nodes.label: Never trust a source-only assertion about a view
nodes.rationale: Source assertions are fine for intent but cannot catch a template that throws when it runs - a Blade fatal (uncompiled @endif@if) and a checklist class the CSS never defined were both invisible to them.

nodes.label: RendersRecommerceViews harness
nodes.rationale: Sets up everything a Recommerce screen needs outside a request: module view namespace, layout stub, module routes, a system table for the global composer, and recommerce.enabled => true - without which RouteServiceProvider::map() returns early and every screen dies on its first route() call.

nodes.label: RecommerceBladeCompilesTest
nodes.rationale: Compiles every module Blade file and asserts the compiled PHP passes php -l and that no directive survives uncompiled, because Blade's compileStatements matches \B@directive and a directive following a word character is emitted as literal text.

nodes.label: Uncompiled Blade directive defect
nodes.rationale: Three pre-existing leftovers happened to balance (an uncompiled @else and its @endif cancel) and merely leaked literal text; two additions broke the balance and made the compiled template a PHP parse error, so two green, mutation-checked, reviewed commits shipped a repair record screen that would have fatalled for every job.

nodes.label: RecommerceDarkPaletteTest
nodes.rationale: Asserts per in-app view that a screen styling its own surfaces references the --sb-* palette and paints no light background outside a print block; print blocks are stripped because they are supposed to be light, and the three layout-less public documents are exempt with reasons recorded.

nodes.label: RecommerceDarkStockComponentsTest
nodes.rationale: Guards 18 stock Bootstrap selectors the first dark pass missed, which measured 1.86-2.04:1 on the dark ground.

nodes.label: RecommerceFormLabellingTest
nodes.rationale: A placeholder is not an accessible name - it disappears on first keystroke and is not reliably announced. Must neutralise Blade -> arrows before scanning attributes and must not flag a control implicitly wrapped in its own label, or it produces phantom findings.

nodes.label: RecommercePublicViewRenderTest
nodes.rationale: Renders the three layout-less public documents and asserts the disclosure limits each page's copy promises - masked serial, escaped customer_facing_update (operator free text over an unauthenticated link, the obvious injection seam), and a QR whose scan target is never rendered as text.

nodes.label: RecommerceRepairRecordRenderTest
nodes.rationale: Renders rather than asserts source, catching both the assignee bug and a dropped trim.

nodes.label: Assignee rendered as 'Assign later'
nodes.rationale: repair/show read optional($job->assignee)->name, but Ultimate POS's users table has no name column and App\User exposes user_full_name, so the record actively reported assigned jobs as unassigned. The trim is load-bearing: the accessor concatenates without trimming, so empty name parts would render as truthy spaces and suppress the fallback. Only real seeded data surfaced it; earlier render passes fed stub data with no assignee.

nodes.label: RecommerceDiagnosticSessionRenderTest
nodes.rationale: Guards labels, order, unit and the raw-key fallback read from template_snapshot_json, so a review pane whose copy promises immutability actually shows what the technician saw.

nodes.label: RecommerceDeviceLifecycleUiContractTest
nodes.rationale: Reads the allowed checklist outcomes out of the controller's validation rule and asserts each generated CSS class has a rule, which is how the outcome-not-applicable gap was pinned.

nodes.label: RecommerceCustomerRepairContractTest
nodes.rationale: Pins that ContactController@create really returns a layout-less fragment, that the intake view uses btn-modal + data-container, that the .contact_modal container ships in the initial markup, and that no target="_blank" remains.

nodes.label: Quick create opened a bare HTML fragment
nodes.rationale: contact/create.blade.php begins at <div class="modal-dialog"> and extends no layout, so opening it in a new tab produced an unstyled form with no stylesheet, validation, select2 or CSRF wiring. The container must ship in the initial markup because app.js binds shown.bs.modal directly rather than delegated, so an injected container would never receive the handler.

nodes.label: SaverposDemoRepairFixture
nodes.rationale: Customer repairs only, on purpose: a customer-owned device carries stock_participation = NONE so the fixture cannot disturb the tracked reconciliation counts the staging smoke is verified against. Rows are written directly and the gate is not touched, because using RepairJobIntakeService would have meant a seeder granting itself the authorization gate - precisely the defect class RC-041 is blocked for. A seeder is a data fixture, not an actor.

nodes.label: SaverposDemoDiagnosticFixture
nodes.rationale: Publishes its template by creating a DRAFT and calling the real DiagnosticTemplateService::publish, so the seeded row passes the same 'only a draft can be published' invariant an operator would.

nodes.label: A fixture must go into both seeders
nodes.rationale: SaverposDemoRuntimeSeeder only runs against a fresh database, so a fixture added there alone never arrives on the already-seeded staging estate; SaverposDemoExpansionSeeder is what reaches it. Both call one shared fixture class so they cannot drift. This is the payment-account lesson repeated.

nodes.label: SaverposDemoRuntimeSeeder
nodes.rationale: Runs only on a fresh database; demoPaymentAccounts() is now the single source of the payment-account shape used by both the fresh-estate builder and the expansion repair.

nodes.label: SaverposDemoExpansionSeeder
nodes.rationale: The path that reaches an already-deployed estate; syncDemoPaymentAccounts fills only missing types so a disabled type or bound account is preserved rather than reset, skips soft-deleted locations, scopes to the demo business, and writes nothing when the map is already complete.

nodes.label: NULL default_payment_accounts blocker
nodes.rationale: Util::payment_types($location) unsets every payment type not marked enabled, and a NULL map decodes to [], so no payment type survives - the 'Cash button does nothing' report was the visible corner of a branch with no payment methods at all.

nodes.label: public/js/pos.js partial payment-account map defect
nodes.rationale: default_accounts && default_accounts[payment_type]['account'] guards the map but not the key, so any location with a partial map throws before a payment row can be built and the button appears inert with no user-visible error. Pre-existing stock Ultimate POS code, out of RC-002 scope, left alone deliberately but owed a decision.

nodes.label: RepairJobController
nodes.rationale: Holds two contradictory disclosure conventions in one file: transition() replaces every message with a generic string while intake() returns the exception message verbatim.

nodes.label: Authenticated 422 disclosure convention
nodes.rationale: Generic transition errors throw away precise, non-sensitive domain guidance; worst is the concurrency message, because a user with a stale expected_lock_version is told only that the transition was rejected and resubmits the same stale form, which can never succeed. Not changed deliberately: the module holds both conventions, and choosing which governs authenticated 422s is a disclosure decision, not a bug fix.

nodes.label: RepairJobIntakeService
nodes.rationale: Drives intake through the real cohort/permission gate; the job it produces matches the fixture's shape, differing only where intended (command_hash), which cross-checks that the fixture is not drifting from the service it mirrors.

nodes.label: RepairJobTransitionService
nodes.rationale: Carries no authorization of its own - the controller does - which is why a seeder may legitimately borrow it to perform state advances.

nodes.label: RepairJobStateMachine
nodes.rationale: assertNewJob is borrowed by the demo fixture so every seeded job is legally formed; enforces evidence gates such as work_submitted for QC and qc_passed plus a resolution code for READY.

nodes.label: DiagnosticController
nodes.rationale: Lists only PUBLISHED template versions matching job type and device category, so with zero templates the screen was unreachable rather than empty. Uses the generic-error convention in both actions, giving the disclosure decision a second site.

nodes.label: DiagnosticTemplateService
nodes.rationale: No UI, console command, or non-demo seeder publishes a diagnostic template, so a genuine business cannot use diagnostics at all.

nodes.label: RepairQuoteService
nodes.rationale: assertWorkAuthorised never fires in practice because no quote can exist to gate anything without a quote UI.

nodes.label: WarrantyClaimService
nodes.rationale: Authorization is correct via AuthorizationGate::allowsWriteLocation; deduplicates on (business_id, command_uuid) under a lockForUpdate on the business row. saleWarranty() was made deterministic by ordering on transaction_sell_lines.id - which line should supply the policy remains a product decision the fix deliberately does not answer.

nodes.label: Warranty coverage start boundary bug
nodes.rationale: The start boundary was strict while the end boundary was lenient (a date-only claimed_on parses to midnight), so a device sold and brought back the same day was refused coverage. Fixed by comparing against start->copy()->startOfDay() rather than setting $start itself, so stored coverage_start_at evidence and the derived term end stay exact.

nodes.label: WarrantyClaimController
nodes.rationale: Referenced AuthorizationException and ValidationException without importing them, so a denied caller got HTTP 500 instead of 404 and invalid input leaked Laravel's field-level validation payload instead of the masked message. It shipped because the only HTTP test for the route asserted the happy path.

nodes.label: WarrantyClaim missing datetime casts
nodes.rationale: The service assigns Carbon so the in-memory model formatted fine and every test passed, but a claim re-read from the database returned raw strings and the card's ->format() would have fatalled. The regression test re-reads a saved claim rather than trusting the instance the service returned.

nodes.label: RepairPartService
nodes.rationale: Reservations do not mutate POS stock - a RESERVED row was written while variation_location_details.qty_available stayed at 1.0000, which is the boundary the module promises.

nodes.label: RepairPublicLookupService
nodes.rationale: Public by design and therefore legitimately gate-free; builds the public status URL server-side, which is why that route looked like an uncalled route in the reference sweep.

nodes.label: Public endpoint token hardening
nodes.rationale: 64-hex opaque token enforced by route constraint and re-validated in the service, hashed lookup with the raw token never persisted, throttled, Cache-Control no-store, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, X-Robots-Tag noindex, and minimal payloads. Escalation to the internal device page happens only after allowsRead plus can_access_this_location.

nodes.label: DataController user_permissions
nodes.rationale: The one exemption in the structural guard: it names all 37 permissions because it renders role-editor labels, so the guard asserts it contains no authorisation primitive and the exemption cannot quietly become a hole. Labels fall back to the raw permission string, so a missing label makes a permission assignable but displayed as a raw string.

nodes.label: status-tones shared partial
nodes.rationale: One tone vocabulary (intake / active / blocked / done / closed) extracted from two divergent copies, documented so a third view maps its own states onto it instead of inventing colours. Exempt from the dark-palette rule because its hues are not in the palette and inventing tokens for them would be worse.

nodes.label: parts/show legend contradicted its own data
nodes.rationale: A 'Parts boundary' legend taught a colour vocabulary the data rows never delivered, so a technician reading both was misled rather than merely uninformed. States were read from RepairPartService rather than guessed, and the legend itself was converted to the same classes.

nodes.label: Measure contrast, don't eyeball it
nodes.rationale: Alpha must be composited up the ancestor chain or the numbers are fiction - treating rgba(255,255,255,0.02) as opaque reported a perfectly readable heading at 1.11:1. Tokens are chosen by measurement: --sb-faint is 3.70:1 on --sb-surface-raised, below the AA floor, so it is decoration only.

nodes.label: Fallback values must be the old light values
nodes.rationale: A CSS variable fallback fires only when the shared stylesheet fails to load - in which case the page is also the stock light theme, so a dark fallback paints white-on-white. Every fallback is the pre-conversion value, so a missing stylesheet degrades to exactly the previous light design.

nodes.label: A uniform anomaly across unrelated pages is your harness
nodes.rationale: An exact 6px overflow on 8 of 13 pages was the preview wrapper's body padding against Bootstrap's fixed 750px container, not a responsive break - a genuine break is not the same number everywhere. The same class of trap made two working buttons look dead when ref-based click coordinates landed off-target; prove the event never fired before concluding a control is broken.

nodes.label: Static guard and rendered audit are complementary
nodes.rationale: The iframe audit found 6 unlabelled controls; the static guard found 17. The other 11 sit behind conditions the fixtures never satisfied. Rendering proves what a fixture reaches; the source scan reaches the rest.

nodes.label: saverbro-dark-pos.css
nodes.rationale: The correct home for app-wide stock component overrides; its byte hash served from the live site was the evidence that proved the auto-deploy had never shipped a commit.

nodes.label: deploy-staging.yml GitHub Actions workflow
nodes.rationale: Calls only cPanel's VersionControlDeployment/create, which redeploys the HEAD of the server's own checkout and never performs Update from Remote, so every push redeployed stale code and reported success. Compounded by curl --fail, which cannot see a cPanel UAPI failure returned as HTTP 200 with an errors array.

nodes.label: cpanel-staging-poll.sh server-local Cron helper
nodes.rationale: Polls the public staging branch internally every five minutes with a lock and a fast-forward-only guard, which is what makes deployment work without touching the protected external cPanel API.

nodes.label: cPanel JavaScript anti-bot challenge
nodes.rationale: API-triggered deployment is unusable because requests receive an HTTP 200 'One moment, please...' page rather than UAPI JSON. Must not be bypassed, disabled globally, or automated - hence the server-local Cron design.

nodes.label: cPanel disables Deploy on a dirty branch
nodes.rationale: cPanel's dirty test counts untracked files, and public/.well-known/acme-challenge/ created by the Let's Encrypt install made the tree read dirty behind a generic message that never named the path. Fixed by gitignoring it rather than deleting it, because the directory is recreated at every certificate renewal.

nodes.label: ICORE_CPANEL_STAGING.md runbook
nodes.rationale: States the required deployment sequence verbatim - Update from Remote followed by Deploy HEAD Commit - which is the half the workflow omitted.

nodes.label: Duplicate logout route name
nodes.rationale: Auth::routes registers POST /logout named logout and a later line registers GET /logout with the same name, so route:cache and optimize abort. Stock Ultimate POS, byte-identical to the vendor import; not patched because someone has to decide which route keeps the name and it is a change to vendor auth routing.

nodes.label: php artisan is broken in this checkout
nodes.rationale: .env sets DB_CONNECTION=sqlite at a path that does not exist, so route:list and migrate fail, while the served app is fine because scripts/saverpos-demo-router.php overrides the connection to MySQL per request. Reconciling .env with the MySQL the router actually uses is still open.

nodes.label: Repeat visit button never worked
nodes.rationale: Three stacked defects: it rendered only in a state where the action is invalid, it was unconditionally disabled inside that block, and its empty hidden command_uuid was stripped by the shared handler before submission so the request could only ever 422. Fixed by gating on the intake permission that assertRepeatAccess actually checks, not the surrounding block's collection permission.

nodes.label: Repair intake customer search endpoint
nodes.rationale: createPage seeded the select with 200 contacts and the search box filtered only those options in the browser, so any business with more than 200 customers could not reach the rest - while an authorized, throttled, business-wide GET /recommerce/repair/customers already existed and nothing called it. Both render paths must re-append the currently selected customer or clearing the search silently drops the selection.

nodes.label: Route-to-caller sweep
nodes.rationale: All 51 Recommerce routes were checked for a reference in any Blade view or JS file rather than assumed to have callers; three had none, one of which was a false positive because the URL is built server-side. This is the check that repeatedly surfaces implemented-but-unreachable features.

hyperedges.label: Implemented services with no UI caller
Staging deployment chain that never shipped a commit
